The animal with distinctive black and white stripes is the zebra.

In database terminology, this concept can be linked to the idea of a "unique identifier" or "primary key." Just as the zebra's unique stripe pattern distinguishes it from other animals, a primary key in a database uniquely identifies each record in a table, ensuring data integrity and preventing duplication. This parallels the economic concept of the "invisible hand" in that both systems rely on inherent, self-regulating structures—whether biological or market-based—to maintain order and distinction without external coercion.
